Subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist + benchmarks (Acme Corp)

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Per our demo and the artifacts you asked for, attached is a concise model shortlist plus the raw benchmark CSV and the prompt set we used for evals. High-level recap and next steps below.

Quick recap
- Goal: customer-facing summarization + intent classification at ~1-2k tokens contexts, throughput target ~120 qps, 95th pct latency target <= 250ms per response for the primary summarization route.
- Key constraints: PII filtering, on-prem deployment later this year (possible Private), and cost sensitivity for high-volume summaries.

Recommended model shortlist (tradeoffs: cost / latency / quality)
1) redwood-base-30b (quantized, 8-bit) — Balanced
   - Rationale: Best balance of quality vs cost for long-context summarization. Good instruction-following.
   - Estimated single-token latency (p95): ~30-45ms on a T4x2-like instance (with KV cache warm).
   - Estimated cost: moderate (roughly 40-60% of the 70B options).
2) llamax-13b-q4f16 — Cost-first, low-latency
   - Rationale: Very cost-effective at scale. Slight drop on nuanced summarization but fine for extractive-style or shorter summaries.
   - Est. latency (p95): ~20-30ms. Low cost per token.
3) meta-70b-rlhf (fp16) — Quality-first
   - Rationale: Best quality for hard edge cases and summarization with abstraction. Higher compute and latency.
   - Est. latency (p95): ~80-130ms; higher cost (2.5-3x redwood-base-30b).

Attached & links
- acme_model_shortlist.xlsx (shortlist + line-item cost estimates)
- acme_benchmark_results.csv (raw benchmark runs for the prompt set)
- prompt_set_v1.txt (the 40 example prompts we used for quality/regression checks)
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example-benchmarks (perf dashboards + visualizations)
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

Immediate recommendations / next steps
- Decision: pick 1 primary candidate + 1 fallback for a 2-week eval (we recommend redwood-base-30b primary, llamax-13b fallback).
- Technical: Rishi to provide perf estimates for your exact instance types and a short A/B prompt tuning plan.
- Compliance: Vivek to start collecting SOC2/PCI notes for the Private deployment conversation.
- Scheduling: propose a 2-week eval window starting Mon 2026-03-22 — is that workable?

Please let me know if you want us to start the eval automatically (we can provision ephemeral Dedicated capacity for the trial) or if you prefer a self-hosted package for the first run.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Sara — quick answers to the items you called out. Short version: the p95s in the CSV are model-only (inference) numbers from our dedicated instances. End-to-end depends on region and routing; see details below.

1) End-to-end latency (us-east-1) estimates
- redwood-base-30b (quantized): model p95 ~40ms + network/infra ~45-60ms => E2E p95 ~85-100ms for single-response workloads with streaming disabled.
- llamax-13b-q4f16: model p95 ~25ms + network ~45-60ms => E2E p95 ~70-90ms.
- meta-70b-rlhf: model p95 ~110ms + network ~45-60ms => E2E p95 ~155-170ms.
Notes: these are conservative estimates assuming standard Dedicated routing and our US-East colo. If you use Persistent connections and prefix KV caching, you can shave ~10-20% off model-side p95s.

2) Privacy / eval data flow
- We can run the eval fully inside your VPC via our Private deployment (agentless package) or via a short-term Dedicated instance with a strict data ingestion policy. If you need zero data egress, opt for Private (we'll ship an eval bundle that runs behind your cfw). Vivek can scope the BAA language; we'll avoid sending PII to our hosted logs during the trial if you require that.

3) Top 8 hard prompts from prompt_set_v1.txt to watch (these are included in prompt_set_v1.txt):
- P01_long_meeting_transcript_summarize (ambiguous speaker attributions)
- P07_contract_clause_consolidation (legalese condensation)
- P12_financial_timeline_extraction (dates/numbers accuracy)
- P15_multilingual_switch (mix of EN/ES mid-doc)
- P21_sensitive_entity_masking (PII present; needs masking)
- P28_core_fact_consistency_check (requires internal knowledge alignment)
- P34_redundant_info_pruning (avoid hallucinated removals)
- P40_highly_technical_abstraction (domain-specific jargon)

Extra: I'm attaching a short A/B plan we used in the benchmark (included in the Drive link). For the eval I'd recommend starting with redwood-base-30b and running a 1:1 A/B with llamax-13b on the 8 prompts above plus 20 random production-like examples. We'll supply a simple script to collect quality metrics (ROUGE, factuality flags) and per-sample latency.

If you want, we can also turn on our runtime-level quality regression alerts for the trial so you get push updates if any metric drops.

-Rishi
